20-university-regulations: This part of the catalogue collects the rules for the 2026–2027 year: policies, personal information, registration, fees, student records, exams and services. It can change during the year.
20-undergraduate: The undergraduate regulations cover general policies, personal information, registration, fees, aid, records, exams, advising, exchanges and graduation. Check them from time to time along with related publications.
20-general-policies-and-information: Keeping up with university rules, and any changes to them, is your own responsibility.
20-mcgill-modalities-of-instruction: Credit courses are in person unless stated otherwise.
Asynchronous: material is prepared ahead and done at a time you choose, sometimes within a set window.
Blended: both online and in-person activities are needed to reach the outcomes.
Distance: you and the instructor are apart and you're off campus; often used to mean the same as online.
Hybrid (hyflex): some attend in the room and others online at the same moment, with equal opportunities.
Online: designed so that being on campus isn't needed.
Remote: a course normally held in person is moved online because of a situation, as in the pandemic.
Synchronous: scheduled live activity, online or in person.
A different modality applies to the whole class, or to a planned subset stated in the outline. It can't be an ad hoc accommodation for one student.
21-authorization-acknowledgement-and-con: Applying means agreeing to follow McGill's statutes, rules and policies, and that obligation runs from registration onward.
Check what you submit: wrong or false information can cost you your admission, and McGill can revoke an offer based on it.
21-student-rights-and-responsibilities: The Student Rights and Conduct site, run by the Dean of Students and the Secretariat, sets out the rules on your rights and responsibilities. The Secretariat's website has more.
21-support-for-students-office-of-the-de: The Dean and Associate Dean of Students lead on advising, academic integrity, discipline, recognition programs and outreach to families and the community.
Office: Brown Student Services Building, 3600 McTavish St., Suite 2100.
21-office-of-the-executive-director-serv: Coordinates all student services and helps with most non-academic matters. Academic concerns go to the relevant person, office or department.
Office: Brown Student Services Building, 3600 McTavish St., Suite 4100.
21-recognition-of-degrees: McGill is a publicly funded institution under a royal charter from 1821, amended in 1852, and incorporated under Québec law.
It was a founder of what is now Universities Canada and belongs to the American Association of Universities and the Association of Commonwealth Universities, among others.
All its degree programs are approved by the Québec government, and its degrees have long been recognized worldwide.
21-language-policy: Teaching is mainly in English, but you may write essays, exams and theses in English or French, unless knowing a language is itself a goal of the course.
To strengthen your English, take an intensive English as a second language course before or as you begin. Continuing Studies and the French Language Centre list options.
Education has special language requirements (p. 691). Continuing Studies students should look at Global and Strategic Communications.
Law: work and exam answers may be in either language, moot courts too, and exam questions may contain material in both whatever the course's language.
Graduate students: see Courses Taken as Extra to a Program in the graduate regulations.
Health Sciences: clinical programs need a working knowledge of both English and French, so see the health sciences language rules and McGill's French proficiency guidelines.
22-academic-integrity: Learn what counts as plagiarism and cheating before you hand anything in. Ask the instructor about referencing, and use Fair Play, the student guide on the subject.
Having unauthorized material in a test or exam is cheating.
Multiple-choice exams are normally screened by computer for unusually similar answers, and the result can be used as evidence in a cheating case under Article 17 of the Code of Student Conduct.
New students must finish an online academic integrity tutorial, in Minerva, during their first semester. Otherwise a hold blocks registration until it's done.
22-policy-on-assessment-of-student-learn: PASL sets shared principles for assessment across McGill's faculties, for equity, consistency and integrity.
It applies to all credit courses, graduate and undergraduate, that end with a grade on the transcript. Units may add their own guidelines if they agree with it.
It's on the Secretariat's website in both languages.
22-policy-concerning-access-to-records: McGill writes to you directly and won't send reports to parents or sponsors unless you ask in writing. Staff can see relevant parts of your record for legitimate use.

Your information is handled under Québec's Access Act and McGill's Privacy Notice. It covers what you submit and your student file: name, contact details, birth date, citizenship, ID, program, status and record.
You can ask to see or correct your information, and object to some releases with an Opposition Form.

McGill may archive your file permanently two years after you finish, exchange data with a home institution, get transcripts from Québec, Ontario and BC bodies, check your immigration and health insurance status with government, and contact you through alumni offices.

It may share data with student associations, schools you attended, professional bodies, ministries, university associations, libraries, funders, other universities if there's evidence of misconduct, volunteers helping you settle in, authorities as required, and McGill's network services.

Referees are told your name, program and term so that they can write for you. Law, Medicine, Dentistry and Music applicants consent to further sharing, such as with LSAC, hospitals or the use of images in concerts.
You accept that admission based on false or incomplete information can be revoked at any time, and that you'll follow McGill's rules once registered. The agreement falls under Québec law.
24-undergraduate-leave-of-absence-policy: Possible for parenting, personal or family health, professional development, military service, or immigration status problems. Travel, time off and money are not grounds.
Ask term by term, for up to 52 weeks in all, through your faculty's advising or student affairs office with documents. It appears on your transcript, and you pay no tuition during it.

You keep your ID, McGill mail and libraries but can't register, do internships or research, and normally can't study elsewhere. After a year without returning you become withdrawn, and you may need to show you're ready to resume.
You should normally be in Satisfactory Standing. Services are limited during a leave and fees or scholarships may be affected, so see Student Accounts and Scholarships and Student Aid.
Health coverage takes arrangements with your student society and International Student Services, and may cost extra society fees. International students should talk to ISS first.
Professional programs may limit leaves. M.D.,C.M. students have their own policy. Continuing Studies has no leaves but allows two missed terms in a row, and a year away means reapplying.
24-health-resources-for-mcgill-students: The Student Wellness Hub is where to get physical or mental health care and advice. Your insurance can be used off campus too.
For barriers caused by disability, injury or illness, see Student Accessibility and Achievement for an accommodation plan, on either campus or in Continuing Studies.
UGME and PGME students go to Medical Learner Affairs. Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Communication Sciences students go to the WELL Office.
25-international-students-non-canadians-: All international students and their dependants must join the compulsory International Health Insurance plan, as Québec and immigration authorities require proof of cover. Rates are on the ISS site.
Private insurance doesn't exempt you, but you may qualify for an exemption request in Minerva with documents uploaded to the IHI portal. It lasts one year and must be renewed.
Minors can register for Québec's provincial plan (RAMQ). Continuing Studies students in credit courses are billed for IHI as well.
25-canadians-residing-in-canada: Students starting in Fall are automatically in their society's (SSMU, MCSS or PGSS) health and dental plan, valid only with provincial coverage or IHI. Studentcare has the details.
Coming from outside Québec? Make sure your home province's coverage stays valid.
25-canadians-who-have-been-residing-outs: Register for RAMQ on arrival if eligible. If not, you may join the IHI plan, but only in the first month of a new semester.
Continuing Studies students have a plan through MACES. Graduate students have the PGSS plan, with a set window to opt in or out.
25-accessibility-and-academic-accommodat: For medical needs, book with the Student Wellness Hub. For barriers from disability, injury or illness, Student Accessibility and Achievement sets up accommodations, possibly with documents, on both campuses and in Continuing Studies.
UGME and PGME: Medical Learner Affairs. Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Communication Sciences: the WELL Office.
25-academic-accommodation-for-pregnant-s: McGill has guidelines on how and when pregnant students and those caring for dependants can ask for academic accommodation in exceptional cases, so that they can continue their program.
26-health-professions-immunization-requi: New students in health care programs, Dietetics and Social Work included, must complete a compulsory immunization program well before classes begin. The Wellness Hub has details.
27-explore-mcgill: A list of the official ways to see McGill in person and online. Undergraduate Admissions has programs, requirements, dates and scholarships.
27-virtual-tours: 360° online tours of both campuses, with menus and optional audio.
27-book-a-campus-tour: A 90-minute guided outdoor walk of the downtown campus with student ambassadors. Doesn't include athletics or residences. Register on the Campus Tours portal.
27-visit-the-macdonald-campus: Guided tours in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, home of agriculture, environment and food science programs. Register through the Macdonald portal.
27-music-facilities: Tours of the Schulich School of Music's downtown buildings and spaces, booked from its Campus Tours page.
27-meet-mcgill-on-campus-and-online-even: Program events and the Meet McGill series are by invitation for admitted students, and may include tours and talks on student living.
27-open-house: Held each fall with tours. Details change yearly, so see the Open House site.
27-start-your-visit-at-the-welcome-centr: In person downtown: the McGill Welcome Centre, 3415 McTavish St., Monday to Friday 10:00–16:00, helps you find tours, admissions information and resources.
27-stay-in-the-loop: Use the Admissions hub to explore, apply and join events. Student-for-a-Day has ended.
28-personal-information: Keep your address, phone and emergency contact current in Minerva's Personal Menu: McGill uses them all year and asks you to check every six months.
Name, gender or birth date corrections need official documents, as set out on Student Records. Macdonald students can do it at Laird Hall, Room 106.
Nursing students need a Québec address and phone number in Minerva for OIIQ registration.
28-submitting-legal-documents: McGill needs documents proving your legal status. What you send depends on your situation.
28-what-documents-does-mcgill-need-from-: Requirements can change, so go by the Legal Documents website.
28-quebec-and-canadian-out-of-province-s: From CEGEP or already in McGill's records: usually nothing. Check your status in Minerva under Student Accounts, View Tuition and Legal Status.
From another Québec university: proof of Canadian status. Québec residency usually needs nothing further.
Born in Québec: Québec birth certificate.
Born in another province or a Landed Immigrant: proof of Canadian status and a Permanent Code Data Form.
Québec resident through another situation: proof of status, Permanent Code form, Attestation of Residency in Québec, and whatever else it asks for.

The Permanent Code form can often be skipped if you've given your parents' names or already have a code. Permanent Residents can use the confirmation (IMM 5292 or 5688), PR card or Record of Landing (IMM 1000). A Québec birth is proven by the certificate or, with a code, a Canadian passport showing it.
28-international-students: Under six months (Exchange, Special, Visiting): a visitor permit or eTA if required, passport photo page and Permanent Code form.
Longer (a degree, certificate or diploma): CAQ, study permit, passport photo page and Permanent Code form.
Forms are on the Forms and Reference Materials page.
29-fee-exemptions: Québec authorizes exemptions from out-of-province or international supplements in three categories.
French courses: full-time international students pay the Québec rate on eligible French courses, with some exclusions.
Out-of-province: non-Québec Canadians in a Ph.D., in postgraduate medical education, or registered full-time in a Master's in French, from when they register and not retroactively.

International, by legal status: citizens of France or of agreement countries, diplomats and staff of international bodies, convention refugees, those awaiting permanent residency with a CSQ, spouses or dependants of temporary workers, and FRSQ-funded students. Some are charged at the Canadian rate.
29-where-and-how-do-i-send-my-documents: Send clear copies by email after accepting and before classes, not originals, with your student ID in each file's name. The Legal Documents site has instructions by category.
29-why-does-mcgill-collect-legal-documen: Your documents set your tuition rate (Québec, out-of-province, international) and confirm your status.

They also get you a Permanent Code, a 12-character code from Québec's Ministry of Education required of all students in the province. You already have one if you studied in Québec. It appears on your unofficial transcript.
Medicine and Health Sciences asks for more documents during admission and registration.
29-quebec-canadian-international-fees-an: Processing takes 5–10 business days. In Minerva, select the right term under View Tuition Fee and Legal Status and read the line saying which rate you're charged.
If you disagree, tell McGill right away. Papers must arrive within the semester; changes are never retroactive, and late ones apply from the next semester.
30-permanent-code: Created or checked by the Ministry, usually within six to eight weeks of your first semester. See it in Minerva. If it's not there, your documents are missing or not yet confirmed.
30-what-are-the-consequences-of-not-prov: The deadline to change your tuition status is the last day of classes, such as December 1 for Fall and April 1 for Winter.
Missing documents after the term starts bring a hold on registering, dropping and sometimes your transcript. International students without valid immigration papers may be de-registered.
30-identification-id-cards: Needed for exams, libraries and services, residences, meal plans and the shuttle. It belongs to McGill, isn't transferable, and goes back to Enrolment Services (or Macdonald Student Affairs) if you withdraw from everything.
Register for at least one course and wait 24 hours. Keep it between terms if you're returning.
Replacing an expired card or changing program is free if you hand the old one in; lost, stolen or damaged cards cost a fee (see Student Accounts).
For access to labs and buildings, ask the building's Area Access Manager. Continuing Studies students wait a day and return the card when withdrawing.
30-id-card-schedule-for-the-downtown-cam: New students can get a card 24 hours after registering for their first course, and returning students any time the centres are open if registered. Student Records lists locations and hours.
30-id-card-schedule-for-the-macdonald-ca: The centre is in Laird Hall, Room 106, in Student Affairs. Same rule: 24 hours after first registering. Dates for new students are on the Important Dates site.
30-legal-name: Your legal name is on your degree, official transcript, e-bills and tax receipts, and is used for your Permanent Code. On admission it's checked against one of the documents below, in this order of preference.

Canadians and PRs: birth certificate or citizenship card (a passport won't do), Record of Landing, a marriage certificate from outside Québec (or a Québec one from before 1984), or a Certificate of Change of Name with driver's licence or health card.
International: study or work permit, CAQ, passport, birth certificate with translation, consulate letter, marriage certificate, or a change of name certificate with passport or licence.
To update: fill in a Personal Data Change Form, attach the document, and email both as PDF or TIFF to permcode@mcgill.ca.
31-legal-sex-designation: Same steps as a legal name: a Personal Data Change Form and an accepted document, emailed to permcode@mcgill.ca.
31-preferred-first-name: Your legal name stays on official documents such as transcripts, reports to government, attestations, diplomas and e-bills.
A preferred first name shows up on unofficial ones such as ID cards, class lists and advising transcripts, and doesn't change your legal name.
Set it in Minerva under Personal Menu, Name and Pronoun Change, as early as you can. You can also ask IT for a matching McGill email alias.
31-verification-of-name: Check your name in Minerva. You can fix case, accents and spacing yourself, but a legal name change needs official documents. Continuing Studies students bring theirs to the Client Services Office.
32-online-distance-programs: Students in fully online programs must declare where they're located each term in Minerva, because location affects fees. Forms open July 16 for Fall, November 16 for Winter and March 16 for Summer.

Studying in Québec means provincial rates by residency; outside Québec, deregulated rates. Self-funded programs pay differently. Some fees, like Athletics, are lower or removed for those away from Québec.

To change a declaration, Continuing Studies students call or email, and others go to Service Point, with proof of location by the last day of classes (August 15 for Summer). After that it waits for the next term.
Falsely declaring you're in Québec can lead to deregulated tuition and action under the Code of Student Conduct.
32-graduate-programs: Online: Chronic Pain Management, Cybersecurity and Healthcare Management (Gr. Cert., 15 credits each), Analytics and IMHL (M.M., 45), Multilingual Digital Communication and Occupational Health (M.Sc.A., 45).
32-continuing-studies-programs-undergrad: Online certificates (30 credits): Applied Cybersecurity, Indigenous Business Management, Public Administration and Governance. Legal Translation (Gr. Dip., 30).

Graduate certificates (15): Data Analysis for Complex Systems, Data-Driven Decision Making, Public Administration and Governance, Public Relations and Communication Management Practice, Strategic Public Relations and Communications Management.
33-registration: After confirming you're coming, register in Minerva in your window and adjust until your schedule is final. The Class Schedule and this catalogue have course descriptions.
Arts and Science have their own pages. New Engineering students must see an adviser during the advising period, and returning ones at the start of Fall and Winter.
Law: returning students choose courses in June, using materials from Student Affairs.
M.D.,C.M. and D.M.D. students register online for prescribed Fall courses. Follow Medical Admissions (Med-1) or the UGME office (Med-2 to 4).
33-registration-periods: Your start time is in Minerva under Registration, Step 1. See When to Register for details.
33-returning-students: Undergraduates register between May 27 and August 14, 2026. Some faculties set their own schedule, so check with Student Affairs.
Law uses rolling priority by year, fourth-years first, set with the Law Students' Association.
Medicine and Dentistry must register for at least one course by August 14 or pay late fees.
33-newly-admitted-students: Some faculties require meeting an adviser first. You may register for Summer before a Fall start. Law students get instructions in their orientation package.
Health Sciences students must register by August 14 and attend the mandatory orientation and registration session.
33-new-students-starting-in-fall-2026: Registration runs June 10 to August 15, 2026. See the start dates for new undergraduates.
33-new-students-starting-in-winter-2027: Registration runs December 1, 2026 to January 5, 2027 without penalty. The DMD Advanced Standing pathway begins in the first week of December 2026. Law and Nursing don't admit for Winter.
34-late-registration: Late registration carries a fee. Returning and new Fall students: August 15 to September 15, 2026. New Winter students: January 6 to 19, 2027.
If you were admitted late and can't register online, your acceptance letter explains how to get special permission.
34-course-change-period: You can add and drop from the day registration opens until the add/drop deadline, which is also the late registration deadline. Winter courses can be changed during Fall too.
After that, adding takes written approval from the instructor and your Associate Dean or Director, plus a fee per course.
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, but talk to an adviser too.
34-dropping-all-courses: Before the end of August (Fall) or December (Winter): you simply aren't registered that term. New students may defer; returning students follow readmission.
After those dates: you're University Withdrawn, noted on your transcript, and readmission applies. Health Sciences students see their own section.
34-course-withdrawal: After add/drop there's a short period to withdraw with a W and a full refund, then a longer one with a W and no refund. Later still, withdrawal is exceptional and never just because of poor work; it shows W or WF without affecting GPA.

It's up to you to do it. Telling the instructor or not attending isn't enough, and the date in Minerva is the official one, even if you stopped going earlier. If you don't withdraw and miss the exam, you get a J.
Required or complementary courses may need an adviser's approval and a form. Music has extra limits, and withdrawals can affect aid, Work Study, immigration status and work permission.

Dietetics Stage and similar internships have different dates. M.D.,C.M. allows changes only on an approved leave. Physical and Occupational Therapy need the Program Director's approval, and Nursing the Director's after the deadline, by written request. Law students are encouraged to see an adviser, and graduate students use a course change form.
34-courses-that-begin-in-the-fall-2026-t: Without refund: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 for single-term courses; Tuesday, January 19, 2027 for multi-term courses starting in Fall, with only the Winter part refunded.
34-courses-that-begin-in-the-winter-2027: Without refund: Tuesday, February 23, 2027 for single-term courses; May 15, 2027 for multi-term courses starting in Winter, with only the later part refunded.
35-class-schedule: Fall and Winter usually appear in Minerva in May, two weeks before registration, and Summer in early February. It shows times, rooms, instructors and any prerequisites or permissions needed.
It changes, so check it when registering and again before classes. The last day of classes depends on a course's pattern (see Important Dates).
Health Sciences students see their faculty's section; M.D.,C.M. students see the UGME site.
35-visual-schedule-builder: VSB shows your possible schedules as a week. It can't register you, but you can copy the CRNs into Minerva.
36-course-information-and-regulations: Courses and programs can change or be cancelled without notice, and not all are offered yearly, so check the Class Schedule.
Graduate, Health Sciences and Summer students have further rules in their own sections.
36-course-numbering: Seven characters: four letters for the subject, then three digits whose first is the level.
100–400: undergraduate, with 300–400 usually for your last two years. 500: senior undergraduates and graduate students. 600–700: graduate only.
Two more characters (D1, D2, N1, N2, J1, J2, J3) mark multi-term courses. Student Records' Transcript Key explains numbers from before 2002.
36-multi-term-courses: Most courses finish within one term. Multi-term versions spread the same content and credits over two or three terms, and you can get credit for only one version.
D1/D2: two consecutive terms, same section, credit once both are passed; registering for D1 in Fall signs you up for D2.
N1/N2: two non-consecutive terms, same section, within 12 months. J1/J2/J3: three consecutive terms, same section.
Arts and Science: registering in different sections can lose you credit, and changing a section in Winter can cause a W on D1, with a fee to reinstate it.
36-important-conditions-for-multi-term-c: Register for every component in the same section, and pass them in order. Credit comes only at the end, with none for part of it.
36-course-terminology: Prerequisite: pass A before enrolling in B. Corequisite: take A with or before B. Credits are in parentheses after the title (see Credit System, p. 52).
36-course-nomenclature-in-program-descri: Required: must be done unless exempt, with no choice.
Complementary: chosen from a set list or area to meet program requirements. They aren't electives.
Elective: usually outside your program requirements, with the most choice. Some faculties allow the S/U option. Graduate students need approval.
37-auditing-of-courses: McGill doesn't allow auditing. Continuing Studies courses can be taken as non-evaluated.
37-course-load: Minerva stops you going past your faculty's maximum. The usual load is 15 credits per term, and fewer than 12 makes you part-time. See Entrance Awards (p. 50) for load rules tied to awards.
37-faculties-of-arts-and-science-includi: New and Satisfactory Standing students: up to 17 credits. CGPA above 3.50: more than 17 by request to Enrolment Services, ideally after seeing an adviser. Probationary Standing: up to 14.
37-faculty-of-engineering: Normally 15–18 credits. More than 18 needs your adviser's permission. Deferred exams (grade L) limit you to 18 credits or six exams a term, whichever is more.

Take enough for visa, aid and scholarships. The (3-1-5) pattern after a description means weekly hours of lectures, tutorial or lab, and personal study. Probationary Standing: 13 maximum, repeats included.
37-health-sciences: Nursing students in Probationary Standing may take up to 14 credits. See your own faculty's section, and the UGME site for medicine.
37-schulich-school-of-music: Normally 15–18 credits. Over 18 in Satisfactory Standing needs permission from your adviser or area coordinator. Probationary Standing: up to 14.
37-courses-taken-under-the-satisfactory-: S/U lets you explore outside your field: one elective a term, to at most 10% of your McGill credits, if your faculty allows.
Apply it in Minerva before the add/drop deadline; you can remove it until the withdrawal without refund deadline. Checking the grade mode and whether the course qualifies is on you.
Instructors grade as usual. A to C becomes S; D, F and J become U. It's out of your GPA, though it counts as attempted, and S earns credits.

For multi-term courses, choose by the first part's deadline. Awards need 27 graded credits, not counting S/U. Visiting, Exchange and IUT students have to arrange it with their home university and McGill's Faculty. Special and U0 Foundation students in Agriculture, Arts & Science and Science can't use it.
Engineering: for Complementary Studies, some Natural Science and Elective courses, not others; D counts as a pass if you skip S/U. Architecture: outside electives only, never toward a minor.
Law: Law and non-Law electives and complementaries, one course up to 4 credits, not for required courses or a minor. Management: not in Minerva, so ask the BCom Office during add/drop.
M.D.,C.M. is pass/fail throughout. Music: non-music electives, not for a major or minor. Not for B.N.I. and B.Sc.(N.) required courses, nor for Physical and Occupational Therapy.
38-first-year-seminars: Small credit courses (25 students at most) for U0 or U1 students of any faculty, with close contact with the professor and advanced methods. You may take one, first-come, first-served.
38-changing-programs-within-selected-fac: In Minerva's Student Records menu, in Arts, B.A. & Sc., Education (B.A. Education and Kinesiology minor only), Management and Science. See an adviser first; restrictions apply.
Minerva can't change your degree or move you to another faculty.
39-faculties-of-arts-science-and-b-a-sc: Foundation students (97+ credits to go): can't change the program, only its options, until promoted.
96 or fewer: change majors, minors and honours in Minerva, with limits.
Science students choose majors or honours only within the group they were admitted to, though any minor. Moving group takes an Intra-Faculty Transfer.
39-desautels-faculty-of-management: Add or change certain programs in Minerva. Confirm limits with the B.Com. Office.
39-faculty-of-education: B.Ed. Secondary students can add, drop or change majors in Minerva.
39-faculty-of-law: Adding a major or minor goes through the Student Affairs Office. Program changes are blocked in Minerva.
39-schulich-school-of-music: Changing or adding a music major takes an Intra-Faculty Transfer in Minerva by the deadline. Double majors, double degrees and minors have their own School pages, and a few music minors are open to other faculties.
39-interfaculty-transfer: Apply through Minerva's Faculty Transfer/Readmission menu unless told otherwise, and check your faculty's rules, documents and deadlines.
International and non-Québec Canadian students pay the tuition for newly admitted students in the new degree.
39-quebec-inter-university-transfer-agre: The IUT lets you register at McGill and another Québec institution at once.
39-mcgill-students: With permission from your faculty, you may take 3–6 credits a term elsewhere in Québec (sometimes a full 12–15), within your maximum load and degree residency limits. You normally need 60 credits at McGill.
Talk to Student Affairs first. The other university can refuse you, and exam or schedule clashes are your problem. Grades there aren't in your GPA or transcript, and late ones can delay graduation.
Exchange students from outside Québec can't use the IUT.
